# ML gold standards — corpus-grounded labels (for approval)

These JSONL files are the **ground truth** the ML accuracy work is measured
against. "98%" is only meaningful relative to a gold standard, so these are built
and **approved before any model is trained**. Every row records its `grounding`
(where the label came from) and a `source`/`confidence`:
`package_stated` | `run_id`/folder | `regex_weak` | `human` | `classifier_candidate`.

Each `*_labels.jsonl` is (re)generated by a committed, read-only builder under
`app/ml/gold/build_*.py` run against `tests/fixtures/dma_packages_batches`.

## A1 Subvertical — taxonomy + corrections (APPROVAL NEEDED)
Codes: `RB CU CL FC IB IC AM RIA CIB` + new **`NON_FI`** (non-financial entity).
- **80 package-stated** (Tier 1, high-confidence, used for training).
- **33 no-stated** (Tier 2, the classifier's real job → held-out scoring).
- **10 human corrections** (grounded rationale in `build_subvertical_gold.py`
  `HUMAN_CORRECTIONS`): Guaranteed Rate→CL, SL Green→AM, First United Bank→RB,
  Farm Credit Mid-America→FC, Chemung Canal Trust→RB, Commerce Trust→AM,
  Navacord→IB, ATB→RB, Mag Mutual→IC, ZipHQ→NON_FI.
- **Still-candidate Tier-2 labels needing your eyes** (classifier guesses that
  may be wrong): `IMA Financial → IC` (likely IB), `SPG → IC` (uncertain),
  `AAA Club Alliance → IC` (uncertain). All other Tier-2 guesses look correct.

## A2 Report-section — curation approach (APPROVAL NEEDED)
The regex classifier confidently labels 386/1801 distinct top-level headings; the
1415 `other` include many real section names it simply doesn't recognize yet
(recurring forms: `issue registry`, `strategic recommendations`, `phased
roadmap`, `peer set overview`, `sentiment overview`, `entity profile`, `pillar
deep dives`, `key strengths`, `critical development areas`, …). Proposed gold =
the 386 confident labels + a hand-mapping of the ~60 most-frequent `other` forms
to canonical kinds (this also fixes obvious regex gaps like "registry" vs
"register"). We do NOT hand-label all 1415 one-offs.
